structuredContent.answer: Low and rising. 3 of 5 PopHIVE signals show influenza increasing in Texas over the most recently available 4-week period (through 2026-10-10) (CDC ILINet: stable; CDC NHSN: stable; CDC NSSP: rising; CDC NWSS: rising; Epic Cosmos, ED: rising). 2 stable. At 10.6% of the 2-year peak as of 2026-10-10 (CDC NSSP). Over the 4w window: rose from 0.3 to 1.3% of ED visits, a +1.0 percentage point change. At this low level, week-to-week changes may reflect reporting noise more than a meaningful trend. The most recent 2 weeks are preliminary and may be revised.

resolved.period: the most recent 4 weeks of available data (through 2026-10-10)

caveats: Preliminary: NSSP and NHSN values for the most recent 2 weeks are subject to upward revision.

NWSS wastewater viral activity is scaled standard deviations above a dynamic baseline, population-weighted to state/national; CDC's Aug 2025 methodology update applies retroactively to all history; updated Fridays.
ILINet measures outpatient influenza-like illness, not laboratory-confirmed influenza.
Kinsa readings come from smart thermometers in near real time (daily); clinical signals such as ED visits and hospitalizations are reported with a 1–2 week lag.
At this low level, week-to-week changes may reflect reporting noise more than a meaningful trend.

Signals CDC NHSN and CDC NWSS show similar recent changes that land on opposite sides of the rising threshold; the differing "stable" and "rising" labels reflect the threshold cut, not divergent signals.
